title: Pasta with Cream Sauce and Seafood

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with cream sauce and seafood is a home recipe that combines tender pasta, a silky cream sauce, and a mix of seafood such as shrimp, mussels, and calamari. The dish is flavored with garlic, lemon, and fresh herbs, while the cream sauce gives it a velvety texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tradition of pairing pasta with seafood originated in coastal regions of Italy, where fresh fish and shellfish are available year‑round.
Cream sauces are often made with cream and white wine, making them lighter than classic tomato‑based sauces.
Seafood is rich in omega‑3 fatty acids, which are beneficial for heart and brain health.
Durum wheat pasta (semolina) retains its shape during long simmering in sauce.
Adding lemon zest enhances aroma and helps balance the richness of the cream.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Seafood (shrimp, mussels, calamari) provides complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s from seafood support cardiovascular health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish supplies B12 and B6 vitamins, important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cream and seafood contribute to bone health by providing calcium and vitamin D.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Garlic and lemon juice contain antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels, or calamari.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Cream sauce adds saturated fats; those monitoring calorie intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improperly cooked seafood can harbor bacteria or toxins; ensure thorough cooking.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Salt and soy sauce are often added, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, garnished with fresh parsley or basil and a squeeze of lemon. It pairs well with a light white wine. Leftovers can be stored in the refrigerator and reheated, adding a splash of cream to restore the sauce’s richness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked pasta in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2‑3 days. Freezing may affect the cream sauce texture, so it’s best to freeze the sauce separately if needed.
